gen-nixie-one-gf-jost: Thin, nostalgic, a little retro-tech: that's Nixie One up top, all open curves. Jost follows in a plain sans with wide gaps at the terminals, so a long page of it keeps moving without clutter.
gen-nixie-one-gf-jura: Jura reads like bent wire, its strokes constant and its s curves opening wide at both ends. Nixie One above it adds a retro-tech heading that shares that thin line.
gen-nixie-one-gf-k2d: Nixie One has a nostalgic, retro-tech feel. It earns its keep when set big and short, while K2D, a tube-like sans-serif whose c terminals hang far from the bowl, handles the rest.
gen-nixie-one-gf-kanchenjunga: Kanchenjunga is contemporary and precise. Its drafting-pen line never clogs at low resolution, though if Nixie One were made small, its fine retro-tech strokes would start to fade.
gen-nixie-one-gf-kantumruy-pro: Nixie One brings nostalgic, retro-tech curves with clear gaps and a line that never changes thickness. And Kantumruy Pro, a sans with an e that opens to the right and no hairlines, stays approachable paragraph after paragraph.
gen-nixie-one-gf-kodchasan: Kodchasan keeps its terminals hanging open and skips any calligraphic thinning. And its easy plainness lets Nixie One's nostalgic, retro-tech curves be the only thing with a past.
gen-nixie-one-gf-koho: KoHo reads wide and open, a plain sans with generous c apertures. Nixie One does the nostalgic display work, with no brush-style swell anywhere, and KoHo handles the text.
gen-nixie-one-gf-kosugi: Kosugi has an open-jawed c like a pair of pliers and a wire-bent look across each word. Kosugi settles into a long passage cleanly, leaving Nixie One's retro-tech heading to handle the nostalgia.
gen-nixie-one-gf-kosugi-maru: Contemporary and tube-lit, Kosugi Maru sets stroke ends far apart in one steady line, like neon, beneath Nixie One's nostalgic heading. It stays plain sans and comfortable going on.
gen-nixie-one-gf-kumbh-sans: Nixie One draws open curves with a constant stroke, nostalgic and retro-tech. It does its best work as a display heading, while Kumbh Sans, a sans-serif with terminals cut short of the bowl, does its best in body text.
